mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05) in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the labor force participation rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which increases perceived risk and depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a single month while UNRATE decreases by >0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: In the identified regime, the 20-day SPX return is positively correlated with both PAYEMS and UNRATE (Pearson's rho > 0.2, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth exceeding 5% month-over-month predicts a near-term surge in consumer and business confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO acceleration and SPX 5-day returns (t-test p > 0.10) in the specified momentum regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the goods price index (CPIAUCSL) below 104 suggests deflationary pressures that reduce expected real earnings for S&P 500 firms, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 104 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During deflationary regime, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 12 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of residential mortgage applications (HOUST) falls by more than 15% in a single month, it indicates cooling credit conditions that prompt the Federal Reserve to hold rates steady, thereby supporting equity valuations and generating positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >15% in a single month relative to the prior month
failure_condition: In lo松ening regimes, HOUST declines do not coincide with statistically significant positive 60-day SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining job openings (RSAFS) while employment remains steady suggests a labor market softening that raises uncertainty and dampens equity risk premia, leading to negative 20-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases for two consecutive months without a corresponding decline in PAYEMS
failure_condition: RSAFS declines are not associated with negative SPX returns in the specified regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer confidence (measured by a composite of survey indices not directly available in the catalog) coinciding with a drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a liquidity rush into equities, producing positive 5-day SPX returns. (Note: Since the exact confidence proxy is not in the observable list, this sketch is omitted and replaced below with a regime-conditional interaction.)
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for the first time in 6 months
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 5 days following UNRATE < 4% (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) shows three consecutive months of contraction below its prior month's level, it reflects supply-side softness that raises input costs and reduces corporate profit expectations, resulting in negative 20-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO contracts for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During supply-side contraction regimes, negative 20-day returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.10).
